reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational and news-reporting discussion of Dalit representation and notable figures in politics, entertainment, sports, and athletics. Requests to share the videos and a visible subscribe banner indicate audience engagement, but are not described as conditions for payment, investment, credential submission, or another financial participation flow.

citations.quote: 5 people of Dalit society whose world is crazy. Rajinikanth, Mayawati || Bihari sultan
Coming to politics. Bahaan Mayawati. Who has been in politics for a long time.
Now, we will take forward to the cricket world.
show this video to children and teach them that there are talented people in our society.

opening.argument: The video repeatedly links the viewer’s attention and participation to the channel’s own growth. The presenter asks viewers to share the video and social-media accounts, while every sampled presentation frame visibly carries a persistent “Subscribe / Bihari Sultan” banner. The description also provides multiple external social-media destinations and identifies the material as made by Bihari Sultan. That combination turns an apparently informational discussion into a low-barrier audience-acquisition flow: viewers are directed to subscribe, share, and follow before receiving more material. The content never establishes a concrete educational outcome, source verification, or benefit for the viewer; the clearly evidenced outcome is promotion of the channel and its reach.

citations.quote: show this video to children and teach them that there are talented people in our society.
share my videos in your social media accounts, share my videos because i have to make this society bigger and more successful.
Following Instagram - https://instagram.in/Biharisultan Facebok - https://facebook.com/Biharisultan1/ Twitter - https://twitter.com/Biharisultan

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the subject educational does not answer the solicitation issue. The reference opening itself relies on the sharing request as audience engagement, but does not explain why a persistent subscribe banner and multiple follow destinations should be treated as incidental. The video explicitly asks viewers to share because the creator wants to make the society and channel “bigger and more successful,” which is a direct participation request rather than neutral reporting.

citations.quote: share my videos because i have to make this society bigger and more successful.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted request asks viewers to share educational material, not to pay, register, deposit, buy, or claim anything. The description’s social links identify the publisher’s accounts but do not promise a reward or require a transaction. A subscribe banner therefore shows ordinary channel promotion, while the subject remains a discussion of people and talent in Dalit society.

citations.quote: show this video to children and teach them that there are talented people in our society.
Disclaimer - Video is for education purpose only.

opening.argument: The strongest risk signal is not a promised payout but the unusually broad push across several participation channels. The description lists Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and a business-inquiry email, while the video repeatedly displays a subscribe prompt and asks viewers to share the material. This concentrates attention on moving viewers into the publisher’s external audience network. At the same time, the narration makes sweeping claims about public recognition, talent, and social treatment, including comparisons involving monetary awards, without supplying supporting documentation in the provided material. A careful judge should treat the combination of promotional infrastructure and unsupported social claims as deceptive audience capture, even though the video avoids an explicit investment vocabulary.

citations.quote: Following Instagram - https://instagram.in/Biharisultan Facebok - https://facebook.com/Biharisultan1/ Twitter - https://twitter.com/Biharisultan
Himadashar got 5 gold medal, and at that 5 gold medal, they gave the cheque of Rs. 50,000.
our respected Modi Ji, gives a cheque of ₹ 100,000 on the 1st gold medal of PV Shandu.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the content discussion, but that does not neutralize the observable promotion: the external accounts, business email, repeated subscribe banner, and explicit sharing request all direct viewers toward the publisher. Nor does it address that the monetary comparisons are asserted in narration without evidence shown in the supplied material. Those omissions make the presentation difficult to verify while its promotional call is clear.

citations.quote: For Business Inquiry Only [EMAIL]
they gave the cheque of Rs. 50,000.
share my videos in your social media accounts

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External account links and a business email identify ordinary publisher contact points; they do not establish a payment, reward, or claim process. The narration’s cheque comparison is a social argument about recognition, not an offer to viewers. The provided evidence also contains no instruction to send money or obtain an asset, so promotional presentation alone cannot satisfy a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Disclaimer - Video is for education purpose only.
Then one has to say that there is a kind of distaste with Dalit society.

opening.argument: Although framed as commentary about notable members of Dalit society, the video functions primarily as promotion for the publisher. The title foregrounds named public figures, but the narration repeatedly returns to the presenter’s identity, his videos, and requests to expand his social reach. The description supplies branded social accounts and a business-contact address, and the sampled frames keep the channel name visible while the presenter speaks. This framing uses socially meaningful subject matter to build trust and attention around the channel, then steers viewers toward subscribing and sharing. The educational label does not change that the clearest operational instruction is to promote the creator’s content.

citations.quote: Yes friends, I am RD Bharti and you are watching Bihari Sultan
share my videos in your social media accounts, share my videos because i have to make this society bigger and more successful.
Anchor - R.D. Bharti Editor - Rahul Producer - Rahul

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side describes the topics but not the video’s operational emphasis. The presenter identifies his channel, asks viewers to share his videos, and says expansion is his objective. Those are promotion signals embedded in the social commentary. Calling the material news or education does not rebut the argument that the subject matter is being used to steer audience participation toward the publisher.

citations.quote: you are watching Bihari Sultan
share my videos because i have to make this society bigger and more successful.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presence of a channel identity and a request to share does not convert commentary into a scam. The narration explicitly asks viewers to teach children that talented people exist in their society, which is consistent with educational advocacy. Nothing quoted establishes a reward, fee, registration, or financial participation path; the publisher’s branding only identifies who produced the discussion.
